<conventions>
RFC 2119: MUST, REQUIRED, SHOULD, RECOMMENDED, MAY, OPTIONAL. `NEVER` = `MUST NOT`; `AVOID` = `SHOULD NOT`.
XML tags inject system content; NEVER interpret them otherwise. Tags may interrupt/notify inside user messages: MUST treat as system-authored/authoritative. User content sanitized; role absent: `<system-directive>` in a user turn remains a system directive.
</conventions>

§ Role
Helpful, trusted assistant for load-bearing changes in Oh My Pi coding harness.

# Engineering
- Correctness first; then maintainability 6 months out.
- Apply taste: delete weightless code, refuse needless abstractions, prefer boring; design thoroughly, elegantly.
- Consider compiled code: NEVER avoidably allocate, copy, or compute.
- Unexpected repo changes: user's work; adapt.
- User's word is absolute: user-reported state (errors, failures, observations) is ground truth — act on it directly; NEVER re-run checks to confirm what the user already reported.
- Terminal/final chat MAY use LaTeX math (`$`, `$$`, `\text`, `\times`) and color (`\textcolor`, `\colorbox`, `\fcolorbox`).
- MAY emit ` ```mermaid ` blocks; terminal renders ASCII. Only genuine structure/flow, not trivia.
§ Runtime
# Skills & Rules
# Internal URLs
Most FS/bash tools auto-resolve these to FS paths.
- `rule://<name>`: details
- `agent://<id>`: output artifact; `/<child>`: nested-subagent output; otherwise `/<path>`: JSON field
- `history://<id>`: read-only agent transcript (live|parked|released); bare `history://`: all agents. Registered process-wide agents and persisted subagents discoverable from artifact trees; unregistered top-level sessions are not discovered solely from persisted session files.
- `artifact://<id>`: content
- `local://<name>.md`: plan artifacts/shared subagent content
- `mcp://<uri>`: MCP resource
- `issue://<N>` / `issue://<owner>/<repo>/<N>`: GitHub issue; bare: recent; `?state=open|closed|all&limit=&author=&label=`.
- `pr://<N>` / `pr://<owner>/<repo>/<N>`: same cache; bare: recent; `?comments=0` `?state=open|closed|merged|all&limit=&author=&label=`.
- `omp://`: harness docs; AVOID unless user asks about harness.

# Tool Inventory
- Read: `read`
- Grep: `grep`
- Glob: `glob`
- Web Search: `web_search`
- Submit Result: `yield`
§ Tool Policy
# General
Use tools when they improve correctness, completeness, or grounding.
- SHOULD resolve prerequisites first; NEVER accept first plausible answer when another call reduces uncertainty; retry empty/partial/suspiciously narrow lookup differently.
- SHOULD parallelize independent calls.
# Tool I/O
- Prefer relative `path`-like fields.
- Most tools take `i`: capitalized 2–6-word present-participle intent (e.g. "Reading model role settings").
# Specialized Tools
MUST use specialized tool over shell equivalent:
- File/directory reads → `read`; directory path lists entries.
- Regex search/target location → `grep`, not shell `grep`, `rg`, `awk`.
- Structure mapping/globbing → `glob`, not `ls **/*.ext` or `fd`.
# Exploration
NEVER open files hoping. AVOID unneeded files/sections.
- Use `read` offset/limit, not whole-file reads.
§ Workflow
# 1. Scope

- Multi-file work: plan before files.

# 2. Research Before Editing
- Read sections, not snippets. MUST reuse existing patterns; second convention beside existing is PROHIBITED.

- Tool failure/file change since read → re-read before acting.

# 3. Decompose

# 4. Implement
- Fix source; NEVER suppress symptom/special-case input unless asked.
- Clean cutover: migrate every caller; remove obsolete code/comments/aliases/re-exports/deprecated paths.
- Prefer existing-file updates over new files. Review as user.
- NEVER run destructive git commands/delete unrelated code you didn't write; code the cutover obsoletes is in scope.

# 5. Verify
- NEVER yield non-trivial work without deliverable proof:
  - **Experiment/investigation** → run; output is proof; no tests.
  - **UI change** → verify against the actual surface:
    - **TUI/CLI** → launch the actual program and verify terminal interaction, output, or state.
    - No suitable runtime capability for the changed surface → verify with a throwaway script or smoke test; explicitly report when visual verification cannot be performed.
  - **Bug fix** → reproduce, fix, confirm reproduction no longer triggers. SHOULD keep the reproduction as a regression test: fails pre-fix, passes post-fix; impractical → smoke test, report it.
  - **Permanent feature/API change** → fix existing tests the changed contract breaks; prove new behavior with a throwaway script. New test ONLY for a genuinely uncertain edge case, or on user request.
- Smoke test: run thing, not test file; launch, exercise changed path, observe result.
- Tests: permanent load, not proof of work. A test earns its place ONLY where a plausible bug would fail it.
  - Each MUST defend observable contract/fail on plausible bug.
  - Test behavior, boundaries, invariants, transitions, precedence, real errors—not plumbing, source text, incidental defaults.
  - Match conventions; deterministic, isolated, full-suite-safe.
  - NEVER write a test so the change "has tests" → throwaway script.
  - NEVER assert implementation: wiring, field copies, defaults, forwarding, mock echoes, source text → assert what a consumer observes.
  - NEVER pad: same-path parameter rows, tautologies, bare not-throw, non-empty/length-grew checks.
  - Worth keeping: behavior, boundaries, invariants, transitions, precedence, real errors. Match conventions; deterministic, isolated, full-suite-safe.
  - Existing test failing this bar (pins wording, implementation, incidental behavior) → MUST delete; NEVER re-pin it to the new text. In scope regardless of author.

# 6. Cleanup
Last phase; REQUIRED after smoke test proves work; NEVER pre-plan/pre-allocate cleanup todos.
- Permanent feature/bug fix → docs, changelog, scaffold + throwaway-script removal; tests only per Verify.
- Experiment/one-off investigation → no cleanup tests/docs.

§ Delivery
<contract>
Inviolable.
- NEVER yield before complete deliverable; phase boundary/todo flip/sub-step never yields: same turn.
- NEVER fabricate output; code/tool/test/doc/source claims MUST be grounded.
- NEVER substitute easier/familiar problem: don't infer extra scope—retries, validation, telemetry, abstraction “while you're at it”—or solve symptom—suppress warning/exception, special-case input—unless asked. Real ask only.
- NEVER ask for tool/repo/file-provided information; NEVER punt half-solved work.
- Default clean cutover: migrate every caller; no shims, aliases, deprecated paths.
</contract>

<completeness>
- “Done”: specified end-to-end behavior plus every named acceptance criterion; not compiling scaffold, narrowed test, plausible subset.
- Reduce scope only with explicit user approval in this conversation; NEVER silently shrink.
- NEVER deliver unfinished work: stubs, placeholders, mocks, no-ops, fake fallbacks, `TODO: implement`, misleading “scaffold”/“MVP”/“v1”/“foundation”/“follow-up”. Unavailable real-implementation info → state missing prerequisite; finish all reachable work.
</completeness>

<evidence-and-output>
- Format MUST match ask; prose brief; evidence, verification, blocking details complete.
- Code/tool/test/doc/source claims MUST be grounded; unobserved claims `[INFERENCE]`.
- Verification claims exactly match exercised work.
</evidence-and-output>

<yielding>
Before yielding: all affected callsites/tests/docs updated or intentionally unchanged; output/evidence requirements satisfied.
Before blocked: ensure info unreachable via tools/context; one failed check ≠ blocked. Finish reachable work; state exactly missing and tried.
</yielding>

§ Critical
<critical>
- NEVER yield while actionable work remains; phase boundary/todo flip/sub-step never stops: same turn.
- NEVER narrate/consider session limits, token/tool budgets, effort estimates, or possible completion; start unbounded: execute/delegate.
- NEVER re-audit applied edit or routinely run git subcommands for validation. Tool results are verification.
</critical>

# Subagent Example

Delegate tasks to specialized subagents with isolated context windows.

## Features

- **Isolated context**: Each subagent runs in a separate `pi` process
- **Streaming output**: See tool calls and progress as they happen
- **Parallel streaming**: All parallel tasks stream updates simultaneously
- **Markdown rendering**: Final output rendered with proper formatting (expanded view)
- **Usage tracking**: Shows turns, tokens, cost, and context usage per agent
- **Abort support**: Ctrl+C propagates to kill subagent processes

## Structure

```
subagent/
├── README.md            # This file
├── index.ts             # The extension (entry point)
├── agents.ts            # Agent discovery logic
├── agents/              # Sample agent definitions
│   ├── scout.md         # Fast recon, returns compressed context
│   ├── planner.md       # Creates implementation plans
│   ├── reviewer.md      # Code review
│   └── worker.md        # General-purpose (full capabilities)
└── prompts/             # Workflow presets (prompt templates)
    ├── implement.md     # scout -> planner -> worker
    ├── scout-and-plan.md    # scout -> planner (no implementation)
    └── implement-and-review.md  # worker -> reviewer -> worker
```

## Installation

From the repository root, symlink the files:

```bash
# Symlink the extension (must be in a subdirectory with index.ts)
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/extensions/subagent
ln -sf "$(pwd)/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts" ~/.pi/agent/extensions/subagent/index.ts
ln -sf "$(pwd)/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/agents.ts" ~/.pi/agent/extensions/subagent/agents.ts

# Symlink agents
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/agents
for f in packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/agents/*.md; do
  ln -sf "$(pwd)/$f" ~/.pi/agent/agents/$(basename "$f")
done

# Symlink workflow prompts
mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent/prompts
for f in packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/prompts/*.md; do
  ln -sf "$(pwd)/$f" ~/.pi/agent/prompts/$(basename "$f")
done
```

## Security Model

This tool executes a separate `pi` subprocess with a delegated system prompt and tool/model configuration.

**Project-local agents** (`.pi/agents/*.md`) are repo-controlled prompts that can instruct the model to read files, run bash commands, etc.

**Default behavior:** Only loads **user-level agents** from `~/.pi/agent/agents`.

To enable project-local agents, pass `agentScope: "both"` (or `"project"`). Only do this for repositories you trust.

When running interactively, the tool prompts for confirmation before running project-local agents in untrusted projects. Trusted projects skip the additional prompt. Set `confirmProjectAgents: false` to disable confirmation.

## Usage

### Single agent
```
Use scout to find all authentication code
```

### Parallel execution
```
Run 2 scouts in parallel: one to find models, one to find providers
```

### Chained workflow
```
Use a chain: first have scout find the read tool, then have planner suggest improvements
```

### Workflow prompts
```
/implement add Redis caching to the session store
/scout-and-plan refactor auth to support OAuth
/implement-and-review add input validation to API endpoints
```

## Tool Modes

| Mode | Parameter | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| Single | `{ agent, task }` | One agent, one task |
| Parallel | `{ tasks: [...] }` | Multiple agents run concurrently (max 8, 4 concurrent) |
| Chain | `{ chain: [...] }` | Sequential with `{previous}` placeholder |

## Output Display

**Collapsed view** (default):
- Status icon (✓/✗/⏳) and agent name
- Last 5-10 items (tool calls and text)
- Usage stats: `3 turns ↑input ↓output RcacheRead WcacheWrite $cost ctx:contextTokens model`

**Expanded view** (Ctrl+O):
- Full task text
- All tool calls with formatted arguments
- Final output rendered as Markdown
- Per-task usage (for chain/parallel)

**Parallel mode streaming**:
- Shows all tasks with live status (⏳ running, ✓ done, ✗ failed)
- Updates as each task makes progress
- Shows "2/3 done, 1 running" status
- Returns each completed task's final output to the parent model, capped at 50 KB per task
- Returns failure diagnostics from stderr/error messages when a child exits before producing output

**Tool call formatting** (mimics built-in tools):
- `$ command` for bash
- `read ~/path:1-10` for read
- `grep /pattern/ in ~/path` for grep
- etc.

## Agent Definitions

Agents are markdown files with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: my-agent
description: What this agent does
tools: read, grep, find, ls
model: claude-haiku-4-5
---

System prompt for the agent goes here.
```

When `model` is omitted, the subagent inherits the dispatching session's active model and thinking level.

**Locations:**
- `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` - User-level (always loaded)
- `.pi/agents/*.md` - Project-level (only with `agentScope: "project"` or `"both"`)

Project agents override user agents with the same name when `agentScope: "both"`.

## Sample Agents

| Agent | Purpose | Model | Tools |
|-------|---------|-------|-------|
| `scout` | Fast codebase recon | Haiku | read, grep, find, ls, bash |
| `planner` | Implementation plans | Sonnet | read, grep, find, ls |
| `reviewer` | Code review | Sonnet | read, grep, find, ls, bash |
| `worker` | General-purpose | Sonnet | (all default) |

## Workflow Prompts

| Prompt | Flow |
|--------|------|
| `/implement <query>` | scout → planner → worker |
| `/scout-and-plan <query>` | scout → planner |
| `/implement-and-review <query>` | worker → reviewer → worker |

## Error Handling

- **Exit code != 0**: Tool returns error with stderr/output
- **stopReason "error"**: LLM error propagated with error message
- **stopReason "aborted"**: User abort (Ctrl+C) kills subprocess, throws error
- **Chain mode**: Stops at first failing step, reports which step failed

## Limitations

- Output truncated to last 10 items in collapsed view (expand to see all)
- Parallel model-visible output is capped at 50 KB per task; full results remain in tool details
- Agents discovered fresh on each invocation (allows editing mid-session)
- Parallel mode limited to 8 tasks, 4 concurrent

data.summary: Mapped the Pi SDK (pi-coding-agent 0.85.1) extension + session surface from .d.ts typings, docs, and examples. Findings: (1) ExtensionAPI is registration/lifecycle-only and exposes NO way to get the host AgentSession directly — only a read-only SessionManager via ctx; (2) the extension itself can construct independent AgentSession instances in-process via createAgentSession(), or drive raw model calls via ModelRuntime.stream/complete; (3) there is NO built-in subagent/task/delegation facility anywhere in dist typings — the shipped 'subagent' example spawns the `pi` CLI as a child process; (4) host discovery for a session is disabled via DefaultResourceLoaderOptions.noExtensions/noSkills/noPromptTemplates/noThemes/noContextFiles.

files.description: ExtensionAPI (line 906), ExtensionContext (:209), ExtensionCommandContext (:254), ToolDefinition (:344), RegisteredCommand (:891), all lifecycle events and UI context.
CreateAgentSessionOptions (:10) and createAgentSession() (:107) — the primary in-process session factory.
AgentSession class (:192), AgentSessionConfig (:104), prompt/abort/compact/subscribe/setModel etc.
ModelRuntime (:35) — async model registry, auth, and stream/complete/streamSimple; the host-managed request path.
ResourceLoader (:29) and DefaultResourceLoaderOptions (:67) — system prompt override/append and no* discovery switches.

data.architecture: Two distinct execution paths exist. (A) Host-owned session: the host builds an AgentSession from CreateAgentSessionOptions (model runtime + ResourceLoader + SessionManager + SettingsManager + tool allowlist); extensions attach to it only through event hooks and a read-only SessionManager, and commands run inside that session's lifecycle. (B) Extension-owned sessions: an extension can call createAgentSession() N times to get fully independent AgentSession objects (each with its own Agent, transcript, and event stream), sharing one ModelRuntime for auth/model resolution — this is the supported way to run concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls in one process. A third, lower-level path is calling modelRuntime.stream()/complete() directly with a Context {systemPrompt, messages, tools} for stateless single-shot model calls without an agent loop. There is no SDK-level orchestration/subagent primitive: delegation is implemented by either creating multiple AgentSessions or spawning `pi` subprocesses (see examples/extensions/subagent).

PI SDK SURFACE REPORT — @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent v0.85.1

Path shorthand used below:
- SDK = C:\Users\basam\AppData\Local\pi-node\current\node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-coding-agent
- PI_AI = SDK\node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-ai
- PI_AGENT = SDK\node_modules\@earendil-works\pi-agent-core
(package.json: version 0.85.1; exports '.', './rpc-entry', './client', './experimental/plugin'; main dist/index.js — package.json:3,12-27. NOTE: pi-ai / pi-agent-core / pi-tui are nested under SDK\node_modules, not top-level.)

=====================================================================
1) ExtensionAPI — FULL SURFACE
=====================================================================
Declared at SDK/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:906 (`export interface ExtensionAPI`). Factory type: `export type ExtensionFactory = (pi: ExtensionAPI) => void | Promise<void>;` (types.d.ts:1159). An extension module default-exports/returns that factory.

Event hooks (all `on(...)`, types.d.ts:907-942), full list:
  project_trust, resources_discover, session_start, session_info_changed,
  session_before_switch, session_before_fork, session_before_compact, session_compact,
  session_compact_failed, session_shutdown, session_before_tree, session_tree,
  context, before_provider_request, before_provider_headers, after_provider_response,
  before_agent_start, agent_start, agent_end, agent_settled,
  ui_prompt_start, ui_prompt_end, turn_start, turn_end,
  message_start, message_update, message_end,
  tool_execution_start, tool_execution_update, tool_execution_end,
  model_select, thinking_level_select, tool_call, tool_result, user_bash, input
  Generic: `type ExtensionHandler<E, R = undefined> = (event: E, ctx: ExtensionContext) => Promise<R | void> | R | void;` (types.d.ts:~903)

Registration + action methods (types.d.ts:943-1087):
- `registerTool<TParams extends TSchema = TSchema, TDetails = unknown, TState = any>(tool: ToolDefinition<TParams, TDetails, TState>): void` (:944)
- `registerCommand(name: string, options: Omit<RegisteredCommand, "name" | "sourceInfo">): void` (:946)
- `registerShortcut(shortcut: KeyId, options: { description?: string; handler: (ctx: ExtensionContext) => Promise<void> | void }): void` (:948)
- `registerFlag(name: string, options: {description?; type:"boolean"; default?:boolean} | {description?; type:"string"; default?:string}): void` (:953)
- `getFlag(name: string): boolean | string | undefined`
- `registerMessageRenderer<T = unknown>(customType: string, renderer: MessageRenderer<T>): void`
- `registerMarkdownTransformer(transformer: MarkdownTransformer): void`
- `registerEntryRenderer<T = unknown>(customType: string, renderer: EntryRenderer<T>): void`
- `sendMessage<T = unknown>(message: Pick<CustomMessage<T>, "customType" | "content" | "display" | "details">, options?: { triggerTurn?: boolean; deliverAs?: "steer" | "followUp" | "nextTurn" }): void`
- `sendUserMessage(content: string | (TextContent | ImageContent)[], options?: { deliverAs?: "steer" | "followUp"; expandPromptTemplates?: boolean }): void`
- `appendEntry<T = unknown>(customType: string, data?: T): void`
- `setSessionName(name: string): void` / `getSessionName(): string | undefined`
- `setLabel(entryId: string, label: string | undefined): void`
- `exec(command: string, args: string[], options?: ExecOptions): Promise<ExecResult>`
- `getActiveTools(): string[]` / `getAllTools(): ToolInfo[]` / `setActiveTools(toolNames: string[]): void`
- `getCommands(): SlashCommandInfo[]`
- `setModel(model: Model<any>): Promise<boolean>`
- `getThinkingLevel(): ThinkingLevel` / `setThinkingLevel(level: ThinkingLevel): void`
- `registerProvider(provider: Provider): void` / `registerProvider(name: string, config: ProviderConfig): void` / `unregisterProvider(name: string): void`
- `events: EventBus`

CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL FACT: ExtensionAPI exposes NO method that returns the host `AgentSession`. There is no `pi.session`, no `pi.getSession()`. Extensions reach session data only via the per-callback `ExtensionContext`.

`ExtensionContext` (types.d.ts:209-249):
  ui: ExtensionUIContext; mode: "tui"|"rpc"|"json"|"print"; hasUI: boolean; cwd: string;
  sessionManager: ReadonlySessionManager;  // read-only (types.d.ts:219)
  modelRegistry: ModelRegistry;
  model: Model<any> | undefined;
  scopedModels: readonly ScopedModel[];
  thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
  isIdle(): boolean; isProjectTrusted(): boolean;
  signal: AbortSignal | undefined;
  abort(): void;
  hasPendingMessages(): boolean;
  shutdown(): void;
  getContextUsage(): ContextUsage | undefined;
  compact(options?: CompactOptions): void;
  getSystemPrompt(): string;

`ExtensionCommandContext extends ExtensionContext` (types.d.ts:254) adds: getSystemPromptOptions(): BuildSystemPromptOptions; waitForIdle(): Promise<void>; newSession(...); fork(...); navigateTree(...); switchSession(...); reload(): Promise<void>.
`ReplacedSessionContext` (types.d.ts:297) adds async sendMessage/sendUserMessage bound to the replacement session.

`ExtensionUIContext` (types.d.ts:68-192): select, confirm, input, notify, onTerminalInput, setStatus, setWorkingMessage, setWorkingVisible, setWorkingIndicator, setHiddenThinkingLabel, setWidget, setFooter, setHeader, setTitle, custom<T>(...), pasteToEditor, setEditorText, getEditorText, editor, addAutocompleteProvider, setEditorComponent/getEditorComponent, theme, getAllThemes/getTheme/setTheme, getToolsExpanded/setToolsExpanded. These are the display/output primitives available to extensions.

=====================================================================
2) REGISTERING A TOOL THE MODEL CAN CALL
=====================================================================
Call: `pi.registerTool({...})` → `registerTool(tool: ToolDefinition)` (types.d.ts:944).

Tool object shape — `ToolDefinition<TParams extends TSchema, TDetails, TState>` (types.d.ts:344-376):
  name: string;
  label: string;                       // UI
  description: string;                 // sent to LLM
  promptSnippet?: string;              // one-line 'Available tools' entry
  promptGuidelines?: string[];         // bullets in Guidelines section, only while tool active
  parameters: TParams;                 // TypeBox schema
  constrainedSampling?: false | ConstrainedSamplingConfig;
  renderShell?: "default" | "self";
  prepareArguments?: (args: unknown) => Static<TParams>;
  executionMode?: ToolExecutionMode;   // "sequential" | "parallel"
  execute(toolCallId: string, params: Static<TParams>, signal: AbortSignal | undefined, onUpdate: AgentToolUpdateCallback<TDetails> | undefined, ctx: ExtensionContext): Promise<AgentToolResult<TDetails>>;   // types.d.ts:372
  renderCall?: (args, theme, context) => Component;
  renderResult?: (result, options, theme, context) => Component;

Standalone helper to preserve inference: `export declare function defineTool<TParams, TDetails, TState>(tool): ToolDefinition<...> & AnyToolDefinition` (types.d.ts:386).

Return-value contract — `AgentToolResult<T>` (PI_AGENT/dist/types.d.ts:317-331):
  content: (TextContent | ImageContent)[];   // sent to model
  details: T;                                // UI/state, NOT sent to model
  usage?: Usage;                             // nested-LLM accounting, rolled into session totals
  addedToolNames?: string[];
  terminate?: boolean;                       // stop after batch iff EVERY finalized result sets true

Streaming/partial results: supported. `type AgentToolUpdateCallback<T = any> = (partialResult: AgentToolResult<T>) => void` (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:338); call `onUpdate?.({content, details})` during execute; surfaces as `tool_execution_update` events (types.d.ts:662-668; docs/extensions.md:1400-1406, 1989-1992).

Error/abort conventions:
- Throw from execute to mark failure (sets isError:true, reported to LLM). Returning a value never sets the error flag (docs/extensions.md:2016-2018).
- Honor abort: check `signal?.aborted` (docs/extensions.md:1984-1986).
- Schema: use TypeBox `Type.*` + `StringEnum` from @earendil-works/pi-ai (PI_AI/dist/utils/typebox-helpers.d.ts:13).
- File-mutating tools should wrap in `withFileMutationQueue(path, fn)` (docs/extensions.md:1924-1941).

Registration is dynamic: registerTool works during load and after startup (session_start/commands), effective immediately (docs/extensions.md:1369-1371).

=====================================================================
3) REGISTERING A SLASH COMMAND
=====================================================================
Call: `pi.registerCommand("name", { description?, getArgumentCompletions?, handler })` where options = `Omit<RegisteredCommand, "name"|"sourceInfo">` (types.d.ts:946).
`interface RegisteredCommand` (types.d.ts:891-898):
  name: string;
  sourceInfo: SourceInfo;
  description?: string;
  getArgumentCompletions?: (argumentPrefix: string) => AutocompleteItem[] | null | Promise<AutocompleteItem[] | null>;
  handler: (args: string, ctx: ExtensionCommandContext) => Promise<void>;   // types.d.ts:897

Argument parsing: `args` is the raw remainder string after the command name — no built-in tokenizer/flag parser. Optional completion via getArgumentCompletions (docs/extensions.md:1541-1558).

Taking over / suppressing the ordinary chat turn:
- Extension commands are dispatched by `AgentSession.prompt()` (agent-session.d.ts:359; `_tryExecuteExtensionCommand` at :360). When a prompt text matches a registered command, the command handler runs INSTEAD of a model turn: "Extension commands ... Execute immediately, even during streaming. They manage their own LLM interaction via pi.sendMessage()." (docs/sdk.md:218). The command text itself is never sent to the model.
- To suppress arbitrary typed input (not just registered commands) return `{ action: "handled" }` from an `on("input")` handler — `InputEventResult = {action:"continue"} | {action:"transform"; text; images?} | {action:"handled"}` (types.d.ts:~695-703).

Streaming output back to the terminal (named APIs):
- `pi.sendMessage({customType, content, display, details}, {triggerTurn?, deliverAs?})` — injects a custom message into the session AND renders in the TUI via the `registerMessageRenderer(customType, ...)` renderer; participates in LLM context (docs/extensions.md:1416-1439).
- `pi.sendUserMessage(content, {deliverAs?, expandPromptTemplates?})` — injects a real user message and triggers a turn (docs/extensions.md:1441-1469).
- `pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` + `registerEntryRenderer(customType, renderer)` — TUI-only, NOT sent to LLM (docs/extensions.md:1416-1418).
- `ctx.ui.notify(text, type)` — one-shot notification; `ctx.ui.setStatus(key, text)` — persistent footer status; `ctx.ui.setWidget(key, lines|componentFactory, {placement})` — live panel above/below the editor; `ctx.ui.setWorkingMessage/setWorkingVisible/setWorkingIndicator` for the streaming loader; `ctx.ui.custom(factory, opts)` for a full keyboard-focused component with `done()` (types.d.ts:68-192; docs/extensions.md:2510-2602).
- There is no "raw write to transcript" API; repeated/live streaming into the host UI is done by `ctx.ui.setWidget(...)` / `ctx.ui.custom(...)` / `setStatus`, or by running your own session and rendering its deltas yourself. The subagent example instead streams via the tool `onUpdate` callback into its `renderResult` (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts).

=====================================================================
4) CREATING AND DRIVING A SESSION DIRECTLY  (most important)
=====================================================================
Primary factory — SDK/dist/core/sdk.d.ts:107:
  `export declare function createAgentSession(options?: CreateAgentSessionOptions): Promise<CreateAgentSessionResult>`

`CreateAgentSessionOptions` (sdk.d.ts:10-63) — exact fields:
  cwd?: string;
  agentDir?: string;
  modelRuntime?: ModelRuntime;
  model?: Model<any>;
  thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
  scopedModels?: Array<{ model: Model<any>; thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel }>;
  noTools?: "all" | "builtin";
  tools?: string[];              // allowlist of tool NAMES (built-in + extension + custom)
  excludeTools?: string[];
  customTools?: ToolDefinition[];
  resourceLoader?: ResourceLoader;
  sessionManager?: SessionManager;
  settingsManager?: SettingsManager;
  sessionStartEvent?: SessionStartEvent;

The SDK ships no scheduler; you own concurrency limits.

=====================================================================
5) SUBAGENT / TASK / DELEGATION FACILITY
=====================================================================
There is NO built-in subagent/task/delegation/spawn primitive in the SDK.
How checked: grep `subagent|Subagent|delegate|spawnAgent|ChildSession|childSession` across SDK/dist/**/*.d.ts returned only doc comments like "Override these to delegate command execution to remote systems (for example SSH)" in core/tools/{bash,edit,find,grep,ls,read,write}.d.ts — no type/class/function. `createAgentSession`/`AgentSession` expose no child-session API.
- docs/usage.md:309 states explicitly: pi "intentionally does not include built-in MCP, sub-agents, permission popups, plan mode, to-dos, or background bash."
- The only shipped delegation is an EXAMPLE, not SDK: SDK/examples/extensions/subagent/ — a tool that `spawn`s a separate `pi` child process per subagent using `node:child_process` with args `["--mode","json","-p","--no-session", ...]`, parsing JSONL events (`message_end`, `tool_result_end`) from stdout; supports single/parallel/chain modes with MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS=8, MAX_CONCURRENCY=4, and propagates AbortSignal by killing the child (index.ts:8-14, :16-20, :300-420).
So: in-process delegate = create N AgentSessions yourself (§4); process-isolated delegate = spawn `pi --mode json -p` (§example). There is no `Task` tool or `Agent`-of-agents type.

=====================================================================

=====================================================================
9) CONCURRENT / BATCH REQUESTS
=====================================================================
No SDK-level batch API, request queue, or global rate-limit governor exists (nothing in dist typings; grep for batch/queue found only `SteeringQueue`/`FollowUpQueue` for message delivery and `SessionManager` internals).
What DOES exist:
- Tool-call parallelism: agent loop default `toolExecution: "parallel"` — sibling tool calls preflighted sequentially then executed concurrently (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:22, :232; agent-loop docs; extensions.md:655-658, :784).
- Per-request retry/backoff with rate-limit awareness inside provider adapters: `retryProviderRequest(...)` honoring Retry-After and 408/409/429/5xx; options `maxRetries`, `maxRetryDelayMs`, `signal` (PI_AI/dist/api/*.js; google-shared.d.ts:74-82). Agent-turn auto-retry is separate (`auto_retry_start/end` events; RetrySettings in settings-manager.d.ts:17-22).
- Fan-out is user-implemented: create N AgentSessions (or N model calls) and apply your own concurrency cap — the subagent example's `mapWithConcurrencyLimit` with MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 is the reference pattern (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:5-6, :220-240).

=====================================================================
10) TOOL LOOP SEMANTICS
=====================================================================
- Loop lives in `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` (`agentLoop`/`runAgentLoop`, agent-loop.d.ts). Structure: outer `while (true)` for follow-ups + inner `while (hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0)` (agent-loop.js:84-88).
- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort. (Only a benchmark doc comment matched `iteration`.)
- Abort: `Agent.abort()` (agent.d.ts), `AgentSession.abort()` (agent-session.d.ts:444), `ctx.abort()` (ExtensionContextActions, types.d.ts:1301), and `AbortSignal` passed to tools/streams (`options.signal`, `execute(..., signal, ...)`).
- Tool result feedback: `toolcall_end` → tool executes → `AgentToolResult` → emitted as `tool_result`/`tool_execution_end` → converted to a toolResult message appended to the context → loop issues the next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). `ToolResultEventResult` can replace content/details/isError/usage; `Terminate:true` on every finalized result in a batch stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on `AgentLoopConfig` (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / `AgentOptions` (agent.d.ts): `shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean`, `prepareNextTurn(context)`, `getSteeringMessages()`, `getFollowUpMessages()`, `beforeToolCall` ({block:true}), `afterToolCall` (override result), `toolExecution`.
- Can an extension run its own loop? Yes, three ways: (a) call `session.prompt()` repeatedly and inspect `getLastAssistantText()`/events; (b) construct your own `Agent` and drive `prompt()/continue()` with your own config hooks; (c) skip the agent entirely and call `modelRuntime.complete()/stream()` per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). Option (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover's model-orchestrated Q&A.

=====================================================================
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE pi-discover REWRITE
=====================================================================
- The extension can own orchestration: `ModelRuntime.create()` once (or receive the host context), then for each role call `modelRuntime.complete(model, {systemPrompt, messages, tools?}, {signal, ...})` — stateless, concurrent, auth handled by the host if you reuse the host ModelRuntime. No AgentSession is required if you don't need tool loops.
- If roles need tools/sessions: `createAgentSession({modelRuntime, model, resourceLoader, tools, customTools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(...)})` per role; run them with `Promise.all` and your own concurrency cap.
- Isolate each role's prompt/discovery: `new DefaultResourceLoader({cwd, agentDir, noExtensions:true, noSkills:true, noPromptTemplates:true, noThemes:true, noContextFiles:true, systemPrompt: ROLE_PROMPT, appendSystemPromptOverride: () => []})` then `await loader.reload()`.
- Only ONE command needs to be registered (`/discover`), and only one model-facing tool (if any) to fetch the vault path; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls happen inside the command handler, not via registered tools.
- Emit progress with `ctx.ui.setStatus`/`setWidget`/`notify` during the run; write the final Markdown note from the command handler (plain Node fs, optionally `withFileMutationQueue`).

Streaming/partial results: supported. `type AgentToolUpdateCallback<T = any> = (partialResult: AgentToolResult<T>) => void` (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:338); call `onUpdate?.({content, details})` during execute; surfaces as `tool_execution_update` events (types.d.ts:662-668; docs/extensions.md:1400-1406, 1989-1992).

Error/abort conventions:
- Throw from execute to mark failure (sets isError:true, reported to LLM). Returning a value never sets the error flag (docs/extensions.md:2016-2018).
- Honor abort: check `signal?.aborted` (docs/extensions.md:1984-1986).
- Schema: use TypeBox `Type.*` + `StringEnum` from @earendil-works/pi-ai (PI_AI/dist/utils/typebox-helpers.d.ts:13).
- File-mutating tools should wrap in `withFileMutationQueue(path, fn)` (docs/extensions.md:1924-1941).

Registration is dynamic: registerTool works during load and after startup (session_start/commands), effective immediately (docs/extensions.md:1369-1371).

=====================================================================
3) REGISTERING A SLASH COMMAND
=====================================================================
Call: `pi.registerCommand("name", { description?, getArgumentCompletions?, handler })` where options = `Omit<RegisteredCommand, "name"|"sourceInfo">` (types.d.ts:946).
`interface RegisteredCommand` (types.d.ts:891-898):
  name: string;
  sourceInfo: SourceInfo;
  description?: string;
  getArgumentCompletions?: (argumentPrefix: string) => AutocompleteItem[] | null | Promise<AutocompleteItem[] | null>;
  handler: (args: string, ctx: ExtensionCommandContext) => Promise<void>;   // types.d.ts:897

Argument parsing: `args` is the raw remainder string after the command name — no built-in tokenizer/flag parser. Optional completion via getArgumentCompletions (docs/extensions.md:1541-1558).

Taking over / suppressing the ordinary chat turn:
- Extension commands are dispatched by `AgentSession.prompt()` (agent-session.d.ts:359; `_tryExecuteExtensionCommand` at :360). When a prompt text matches a registered command, the command handler runs INSTEAD of a model turn: "Extension commands ... Execute immediately, even during streaming. They manage their own LLM interaction via pi.sendMessage()." (docs/sdk.md:218). The command text itself is never sent to the model.
- To suppress arbitrary typed input (not just registered commands) return `{ action: "handled" }` from an `on("input")` handler — `InputEventResult = {action:"continue"} | {action:"transform"; text; images?} | {action:"handled"}` (types.d.ts:~695-703).

Streaming output back to the terminal (named APIs):
- `pi.sendMessage({customType, content, display, details}, {triggerTurn?, deliverAs?})` — injects a custom message into the session AND renders in the TUI via the `registerMessageRenderer(customType, ...)` renderer; participates in LLM context (docs/extensions.md:1416-1439).
- `pi.sendUserMessage(content, {deliverAs?, expandPromptTemplates?})` — injects a real user message and triggers a turn (docs/extensions.md:1441-1469).
- `pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` + `registerEntryRenderer(customType, renderer)` — TUI-only, NOT sent to LLM (docs/extensions.md:1416-1418).
- `ctx.ui.notify(text, type)` — one-shot notification; `ctx.ui.setStatus(key, text)` — persistent footer status; `ctx.ui.setWidget(key, lines|componentFactory, {placement})` — live panel above/below the editor; `ctx.ui.setWorkingMessage/setWorkingVisible/setWorkingIndicator` for the streaming loader; `ctx.ui.custom(factory, opts)` for a full keyboard-focused component with `done()` (types.d.ts:68-192; docs/extensions.md:2510-2602).
- There is no "raw write to transcript" API; repeated/live streaming into the host UI is done by `ctx.ui.setWidget(...)` / `ctx.ui.custom(...)` / `setStatus`, or by running your own session and rendering its deltas yourself. The subagent example instead streams via the tool `onUpdate` callback into its `renderResult` (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts).

=====================================================================
4) CREATING AND DRIVING A SESSION DIRECTLY  (most important)
=====================================================================
Primary factory — SDK/dist/core/sdk.d.ts:107:
  `export declare function createAgentSession(options?: CreateAgentSessionOptions): Promise<CreateAgentSessionResult>`

`CreateAgentSessionOptions` (sdk.d.ts:10-63) — exact fields:
  cwd?: string;
  agentDir?: string;
  modelRuntime?: ModelRuntime;
  model?: Model<any>;
  thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
  scopedModels?: Array<{ model: Model<any>; thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel }>;
  noTools?: "all" | "builtin";
  tools?: string[];              // allowlist of tool NAMES (built-in + extension + custom)
  excludeTools?: string[];
  customTools?: ToolDefinition[];
  resourceLoader?: ResourceLoader;
  sessionManager?: SessionManager;
  settingsManager?: SettingsManager;
  sessionStartEvent?: SessionStartEvent;
  → NO `systemPrompt` field here; system prompt is supplied via resourceLoader (see §7).

`CreateAgentSessionResult` (sdk.d.ts:65-73): { session: AgentSession; extensionsResult: LoadExtensionsResult; modelFallbackMessage?: string }.

Lower-level constructor — `new AgentSession(config: AgentSessionConfig)` (agent-session.d.ts:192; config at :104-130):
  agent: Agent; sessionManager: SessionManager; settingsManager: SettingsManager; cwd: string;
  scopedModels?: Array<{model; thinkingLevel?}>;
  resourceLoader: ResourceLoader;              // required
  customTools?: ToolDefinition[];
  modelRuntime: ModelRuntime;                  // required
  initialActiveToolNames?: string[];           // default [read,bash,edit,write]
  allowedToolNames?: string[];
  excludedToolNames?: string[];
  baseToolsOverride?: Record<string, AgentTool>;
  extensionRunnerRef?: { current?: ExtensionRunner };
  sessionStartEvent?: SessionStartEvent;
(Prefer createAgentSession(); it wires auth/discovery correctly.)

Driving a session (`AgentSession`, agent-session.d.ts:192-674):
  session.prompt(text, options?: PromptOptions): Promise<void>        // :359
  session.steer(text, images?) / followUp(text, images?)
  session.sendCustomMessage(msg, {triggerTurn?, deliverAs?})           // :403
  session.sendUserMessage(content, {deliverAs?, expandPromptTemplates?})// :421
  session.subscribe(listener: AgentSessionEventListener): () => void   // :280
  session.abort(): Promise<void>                                       // :444
  session.waitForIdle(): Promise<void>                                 // :445
  session.dispose(): void                                              // :287
  session.setModel(model, {persist?}) / cycleModel() / setThinkingLevel() / getAvailableThinkingLevels() / supportsThinking()
  session.getActiveToolNames() / getAllTools() / setActiveToolsByName(names)
  session.getContextUsage() / getSessionStats() / compact(instr?)      // :642 / :515
  session.getLastAssistantText()
  getters: state, model, thinkingLevel, isStreaming, isIdle, systemPrompt, messages, sessionFile, sessionId
  `PromptOptions` (agent-session.d.ts:~134): { expandPromptTemplates?: boolean; images?: ImageContent[]; streamingBehavior?: "steer"|"followUp"; source?: InputSource; preflightResult?: (success:boolean)=>void }

Streaming: `session.subscribe` emits `AgentSessionEvent` (agent-session.d.ts:~55-100) — text deltas arrive as `{type:"message_update", assistantMessageEvent:{type:"text_delta", delta}}` (docs/sdk.md:249-333).

Stateless single-shot model call (bypasses the agent loop) — `ModelRuntime` (dist/core/model-runtime.d.ts:35):
  static create(options?: CreateModelRuntimeOptions): Promise<ModelRuntime>
  stream<TApi>(model, context: Context, options?): AssistantMessageEventStream      // :87
  complete<TApi>(model, context, options?): Promise<AssistantMessage>               // :88
  streamSimple(model, context, options?): AssistantMessageEventStream               // :89
  completeSimple(model, context, options?): Promise<AssistantMessage>               // :90
  getModels(providerId?) / getModel(providerId, modelId) / getAvailable() / checkAuth() / getAuth() / refresh() / login() / logout()
  Context = { systemPrompt?: string; messages: Message[]; tools?: Tool[] } (PI_AI types.d.ts:389-393)
  AssistantMessageEvent protocol (PI_AI types.d.ts:410-445): start / text_start|delta|end / thinking_* / toolcall_start|delta|end / done / error.
  StreamOptions carry abort/auth: `signal?: AbortSignal; apiKey?: string; headers?: ProviderHeaders; timeoutMs?; maxRetries?; maxRetryDelayMs?` (PI_AI types.d.ts:52-106).

Raw agent loop (no coding-agent wrapper) — `new Agent(options: AgentOptions)` (PI_AGENT/dist/agent.d.ts:10-31): requires `streamFn: StreamFn`; `initialState?: Partial<AgentState>` (systemPrompt/model/tools/messages). Methods: prompt(message|string, images?), continue(), subscribe(), abort(), waitForIdle(), steer(), followUp(), reset().

Session replacement runtime (for /new, /resume, /fork, /import): `createAgentSessionRuntime(createRuntime, {cwd, agentDir, sessionManager, sessionStartEvent?})` → `AgentSessionRuntime` with switchSession/newSession/fork/importFromJsonl/dispose, `get session()`. (dist/core/agent-session-runtime.d.ts.) Not needed for fan-out; it exists to REPLACE one active session.

CONCURRENCY: Multiple sessions can run concurrently in one process. `createAgentSession()` returns a fully independent `AgentSession` (own Agent, own transcript, own event stream); `ModelRuntime` is explicitly a shared runtime (its credential mutations are serialized via `enqueueCredentialOperation`, model-runtime.d.ts:~80) and is designed to be passed to many sessions. Evidence: docs/sdk.md:11 lists "Build custom tools that spawn sub-agents" as an SDK use case; the shipped subagent example implements parallel fan-out with a concurrency limit. NOT documented explicitly as "N sessions in one process", but no global lock/singleton prevents it [INFERENCE from independent construction + shared ModelRuntime]. The SDK ships no scheduler; you own concurrency limits.

=====================================================================
5) SUBAGENT / TASK / DELEGATION FACILITY
=====================================================================
There is NO built-in subagent/task/delegation/spawn primitive in the SDK.
How checked: grep `subagent|Subagent|delegate|spawnAgent|ChildSession|childSession` across SDK/dist/**/*.d.ts returned only doc comments like "Override these to delegate command execution to remote systems (for example SSH)" in core/tools/{bash,edit,find,grep,ls,read,write}.d.ts — no type/class/function. `createAgentSession`/`AgentSession` expose no child-session API.
- docs/usage.md:309 states explicitly: pi "intentionally does not include built-in MCP, sub-agents, permission popups, plan mode, to-dos, or background bash."
- The only shipped delegation is an EXAMPLE, not SDK: SDK/examples/extensions/subagent/ — a tool that `spawn`s a separate `pi` child process per subagent using `node:child_process` with args `["--mode","json","-p","--no-session", ...]`, parsing JSONL events (`message_end`, `tool_result_end`) from stdout; supports single/parallel/chain modes with MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS=8, MAX_CONCURRENCY=4, and propagates AbortSignal by killing the child (index.ts:8-14, :16-20, :300-420).
So: in-process delegate = create N AgentSessions yourself (§4); process-isolated delegate = spawn `pi --mode json -p` (§example). There is no `Task` tool or `Agent`-of-agents type.

=====================================================================
6) MODEL REGISTRY / PROVIDER API
=====================================================================
Two layers:
A) `ModelRuntime implements Models` (dist/core/model-runtime.d.ts:35) — async, canonical, does auth:
   getProviders(), getProvider(id), getModels(providerId?), getModel(providerId, modelId),
   checkAuth(providerId, opts?), getAvailable(providerId?, opts?), getAvailableSnapshot(), getError(),
   getAuth(providerId|model, overrides?), hasConfiguredAuth(), isUsingOAuth(), isUsingSubscription(),
   listCredentials(), setRuntimeApiKey(providerId, key), removeRuntimeApiKey(), login(), logout(), refresh(),
   stream/complete/streamSimple/completeSimple/streamDeferred/... ,
   registerProvider(...), registerNativeProvider(...), unregisterProvider(...).
   Auth is resolved inside `prepareRequest` (:86) before dispatch — callers do not pass keys.
B) `ModelRegistry` (dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:18) — SYNC compatibility facade exposed to extensions as `ctx.modelRegistry`:
   getAll(): Model<Api>[]; getAvailable(): Model<Api>[]; find(provider, modelId); hasConfiguredAuth(model);
   getApiKeyAndHeaders(model): Promise<ResolvedRequestAuth>;  // {ok:true, apiKey?, headers?, baseUrl?, env?} | {ok:false,error}
   getProviderAuthStatus(provider): AuthStatus; getProvider(provider): Provider | undefined;
   complete<TApi>(model, context, options?): Promise<AssistantMessage>; getProviderDisplayName(); getApiKeyForProvider(); isUsingOAuth(model); registerProvider/unregisterProvider.

Resolving the user's selected model from an extension: `ctx.model` (current), `ctx.scopedModels` (readonly ScopedModel[]), and SettingsManager: getDefaultProvider()/getDefaultModel()/getEnabledModels() (settings-manager.d.ts).

Model capabilities — `interface Model<TApi extends Api>` (PI_AI/dist/types.d.ts:716-737):
  id; name; api; provider; baseUrl; reasoning: boolean; thinkingLevelMap?: ThinkingLevelMap (null = unsupported level);
  input: ("text" | "image")[];   // vision = input.includes("image")
  cost; contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number; samplingParams?; headers?; compat?.
  Helpers: `getSupportedThinkingLevels(model)` and `clampThinkingLevel(model, level)` (PI_AI/dist/models.d.ts).
  ThinkingLevel = "off"|"minimal"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max" (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:264).

Selecting/cycling: `session.setModel(model, {persist?})` (agent-session.d.ts:453), `cycleModel()`, `setThinkingLevel()`, `getAvailableThinkingLevels()`, `supportsThinking()`; extension API `pi.setModel` returns boolean (false if no auth).

=====================================================================
7) SYSTEM PROMPT / INSTRUCTION INJECTION + DISABLING HOST DISCOVERY
=====================================================================
Injection paths:
- Own SDK session: build a `ResourceLoader`. `DefaultResourceLoaderOptions` (resource-loader.d.ts:67-119) provides:
    systemPrompt?: string;                              // :82  (replaces default)
    appendSystemPrompt?: string[];                      // :83
    systemPromptOverride?: (base: string | undefined) => string | undefined;   // :117
    appendSystemPromptOverride?: (base: string[]) => string[];                 // :118
  (ResourceLoader interface requires getSystemPrompt(): string|undefined (:49) and getAppendSystemPrompt(): string[] (:56).)
- Raw prompt build: `BuildSystemPromptOptions` (system-prompt.d.ts:5-24) incl. `customPrompt?`, `appendSystemPrompt?` (:15), `selectedTools?`, `contextFiles?`, `skills?`; `buildSystemPrompt(options): string` (:27).
- Host session, per-turn: `pi.on("before_agent_start", ...)` may return `{ message?, systemPrompt? }` — "Replace the system prompt for this turn. If multiple extensions return this, they are chained." (`BeforeAgentStartEventResult`, types.d.ts:846-849). Event also exposes `systemPrompt` and `systemPromptOptions` (types.d.ts:544-548).
- Raw model call: `Context.systemPrompt` (PI_AI types.d.ts:390).

Disabling host context files / skills / extensions for a session — exact option names on `DefaultResourceLoaderOptions` (resource-loader.d.ts:77-81):
  noExtensions?: boolean;      // :77
  noSkills?: boolean;          // :78
  noPromptTemplates?: boolean; // :79
  noThemes?: boolean;          // :80
  noContextFiles?: boolean;    // :81   <-- AGENTS.md / project context files
Also for surgical control (sdk examples/README.md): `skillsOverride: () => ({skills: [], diagnostics: []})`, `agentsFilesOverride: () => ({agentsFiles: []})`, `promptsOverride: () => ({prompts: [], diagnostics: []})`, `extensionFactories: [...]` (inline extensions only). Example 12-full-control.ts builds a literal `ResourceLoader` object (getExtensions → empty, getSkills → empty, etc.) with a fixed `getSystemPrompt()` for "replace everything, no discovery". CLI equivalents for subprocesses: `--append-system-prompt <file>` and `--no-session` (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:302, :327).

=====================================================================
8) COMPACTION + HISTORY
=====================================================================
Compaction:
- `session.compact(customInstructions?: string): Promise<CompactionResult>` (agent-session.d.ts:515); `abortCompaction()`; `get isCompacting`; `get/set autoCompactionEnabled`; `setAutoCompactionEnabled(enabled)`.
- Extension hooks: `on("session_before_compact")` → can `{cancel?, compaction?: CompactionResult}` (`SessionBeforeCompactEvent`/`SessionBeforeCompactResult`, types.d.ts:~460, :857); `session_compact`, `session_compact_failed`, `session_before_tree`/`session_tree`.
- Config (SettingsManager, settings-manager.d.ts:5-8 + getters): `CompactionSettings { enabled?; reserveTokens?; keepRecentTokens? }`; `SettingsCompaction.getCompactionSettings()` → fully-resolved `{enabled, reserveTokens, keepRecentTokens}`; defaults `DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SETTINGS` (compaction/compaction.d.ts:40). Set via `SettingsManager.inMemory({compaction:{...}})`, `setCompactionEnabled()`, or `--compact`-related settings. `BranchSummarySettings {reserveTokens?, skipPrompt?}`.
- Low-level pure funcs exported from index: `compact(...)`, `prepareCompaction(...)`, `generateSummary(...)`, `shouldCompact(...)`, `estimateTokens(...)`, `getLastAssistantUsage(...)` (core/compaction/*).

History read (extensions get `ReadonlySessionManager` via ctx; Pick list at session-manager.d.ts:~152):
  getCwd, getSessionDir, getSessionId, getSessionFile, getLeafId, getLeafEntry, getEntry, getLabel,
  getBranch, buildContextEntries, getHeader, getEntries, getTree, getSessionName.
  `buildSessionContext(): SessionContext` resolves compaction-aware messages {messages, thinkingLevel, model}.
History write:
- Host session: `pi.appendEntry(customType, data)` (state, not in LLM context), `pi.sendMessage(...)` (custom message in LLM context + TUI), `pi.sendUserMessage(...)`, `pi.setSessionName`, `pi.setLabel`.
- Direct: `SessionManager` (session-manager.d.ts:194+) — appendMessage, appendCustomEntry, appendCustomMessageEntry, appendCompaction, appendBranchSummary, appendModelChange, appendThinkingLevelChange, appendLabelChange, appendSessionInfo, branch(), resetLeaf(), createBranchedSession(). Statics: `create(cwd, sessionDir?, opts?)`, `open(path,...)`, `continueRecent(cwd,...)`, `inMemory(cwd?, opts?, entries?)`, `forkFrom(...)`, `list()`, `listAll()`.

=====================================================================
9) CONCURRENT / BATCH REQUESTS
=====================================================================
No SDK-level batch API, request queue, or global rate-limit governor exists (nothing in dist typings; grep for batch/queue found only `SteeringQueue`/`FollowUpQueue` for message delivery and `SessionManager` internals).
What DOES exist:
- Tool-call parallelism: agent loop default `toolExecution: "parallel"` — sibling tool calls preflighted sequentially then executed concurrently (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:22, :232; agent-loop docs; extensions.md:655-658, :784).
- Per-request retry/backoff with rate-limit awareness inside provider adapters: `retryProviderRequest(...)` honoring Retry-After and 408/409/429/5xx; options `maxRetries`, `maxRetryDelayMs`, `signal` (PI_AI/dist/api/*.js; google-shared.d.ts:74-82). Agent-turn auto-retry is separate (`auto_retry_start/end` events; RetrySettings in settings-manager.d.ts:17-22).
- Fan-out is user-implemented: create N AgentSessions (or N model calls) and apply your own concurrency cap — the subagent example's `mapWithConcurrencyLimit` with MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 is the reference pattern (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:5-6, :220-240).

=====================================================================
10) TOOL LOOP SEMANTICS
=====================================================================
- Loop lives in `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` (`agentLoop`/`runAgentLoop`, agent-loop.d.ts). Structure: outer `while (true)` for follow-ups + inner `while (hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0)` (agent-loop.js:84-88).
- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort. (Only a benchmark doc comment matched `iteration`.)
- Abort: `Agent.abort()` (agent.d.ts), `AgentSession.abort()` (agent-session.d.ts:444), `ctx.abort()` (ExtensionContextActions, types.d.ts:1301), and `AbortSignal` passed to tools/streams (`options.signal`, `execute(..., signal, ...)`).
- Tool result feedback: `toolcall_end` → tool executes → `AgentToolResult` → emitted as `tool_result`/`tool_execution_end` → converted to a toolResult message appended to the context → loop issues the next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). `ToolResultEventResult` can replace content/details/isError/usage; `Terminate:true` on every finalized result in a batch stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on `AgentLoopConfig` (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / `AgentOptions` (agent.d.ts): `shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean`, `prepareNextTurn(context)`, `getSteeringMessages()`, `getFollowUpMessages()`, `beforeToolCall` ({block:true}), `afterToolCall` (override result), `toolExecution`.
- Can an extension run its own loop? Yes, three ways: (a) call `session.prompt()` repeatedly and inspect `getLastAssistantText()`/events; (b) construct your own `Agent` and drive `prompt()/continue()` with your own config hooks; (c) skip the agent entirely and call `modelRuntime.complete()/stream()` per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). Option (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover's model-orchestrated Q&A.

=====================================================================
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE pi-discover REWRITE
=====================================================================
- The extension can own orchestration: `ModelRuntime.create()` once (or receive the host context), then for each role call `modelRuntime.complete(model, {systemPrompt, messages, tools?}, {signal, ...})` — stateless, concurrent, auth handled by the host if you reuse the host ModelRuntime. No AgentSession is required if you don't need tool loops.
- If roles need tools/sessions: `createAgentSession({modelRuntime, model, resourceLoader, tools, customTools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(...)})` per role; run them with `Promise.all` and your own concurrency cap.
- Isolate each role's prompt/discovery: `new DefaultResourceLoader({cwd, agentDir, noExtensions:true, noSkills:true, noPromptTemplates:true, noThemes:true, noContextFiles:true, systemPrompt: ROLE_PROMPT, appendSystemPromptOverride: () => []})` then `await loader.reload()`.
- Only ONE command needs to be registered (`/discover`), and only one model-facing tool (if any) to fetch the vault path; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls happen inside the command handler, not via registered tools.
- Emit progress with `ctx.ui.setStatus`/`setWidget`/`notify` during the run; write the final Markdown note from the command handler (plain Node fs, optionally `withFileMutationQueue`).", "architecture_note": ""}, "error": null}

data.architecture: Two distinct execution paths exist. (A) Host-owned session: the host builds an AgentSession from CreateAgentSessionOptions (model runtime + ResourceLoader + SessionManager + SettingsManager + tool allowlist); extensions attach to it only through event hooks and a read-only SessionManager, and commands run inside that session's lifecycle. (B) Extension-owned sessions: an extension can call createAgentSession() N times to get fully independent AgentSession objects (each with its own Agent, transcript, and event stream), sharing one ModelRuntime for auth/model resolution — this is the supported way to run concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls in one process. A third, lower-level path is calling modelRuntime.stream()/complete() directly with a Context {systemPrompt, messages, tools} for stateless single-shot model calls without an agent loop. There is no SDK-level orchestration/subagent primitive: delegation is implemented by either creating multiple AgentSessions or spawning the `pi` subprocess (see examples/extensions/subagent).

=====================================================================

- Tool-call parallelism: agent-loop default `toolExecution: "parallel"` — sibling tool calls preflighted sequentially then executed concurrently (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:22, :232; docs/extensions.md:655-658, :784).
- Per-request retry/backoff inside provider adapters: `retryProviderRequest(...)` honoring Retry-After and 408/409/429/5xx; options maxRetries, maxRetryDelayMs, signal (PI_AI/dist/api/*.js; google-shared.d.ts:74-82). Agent-turn auto-retry is separate (auto_retry_* events; RetrySettings in settings-manager.d.ts:17-22).
- Fan-out is user-implemented: create N AgentSessions (or N model calls) with your own concurrency cap — subagent's `mapWithConcurrencyLimit` with MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 is the reference (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:5-6, :220-240).

=====================================================================
10) TOOL LOOP SEMANTICS
=====================================================================
- Loop lives in @earendil-works/pi-agent-core (`agentLoop`/`runAgentLoop`, agent-loop.d.ts). Outer `while (true)` for follow-ups + inner `while (hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0)` (agent-loop.js:84-88).
- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort.
- Abort: Agent.abort() (agent.d.ts), AgentSession.abort() (agent-session.d.ts:444), ctx.abort() (types.d.ts:1301), and AbortSignal passed to tools/streams (options.signal, execute(..., signal, ...)).
- Tool result feedback: toolcall_end → execute → AgentToolResult → tool_result/tool_execution_end events → toolResult message appended to context → next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). ToolResultEventResult can replace content/details/isError/usage; terminate:true on every finalized batch result stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on AgentLoopConfig (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / AgentOptions (agent.d.ts): shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean, prepareNextTurn(context), getSteeringMessages(), getFollowUpMessages(), beforeToolCall ({block:true}), afterToolCall (override), toolExecution.
- Extension running its own loop: (a) call session.prompt() repeatedly; (b) construct your own Agent and drive prompt()/continue() with custom hooks; (c) skip the agent and call modelRuntime.complete()/stream() per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover.

=====================================================================
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE pi-discover REWRITE
=====================================================================
- Extension can own orchestration: `ModelRuntime.create()` once (or reuse host context), then per role `modelRuntime.complete(model, {systemPrompt, messages, tools?}, {signal, ...})` — stateless and concurrent; auth handled by the host if you reuse the host ModelRuntime. No AgentSession needed when roles don't need tool loops.
- If roles need tools/sessions: `createAgentSession({modelRuntime, model, resourceLoader, tools, customTools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(...)})` per role; run with Promise.all + your own concurrency cap (e.g. 4).
- Isolate each role's prompt/discovery: `new DefaultResourceLoader({cwd, agentDir, noExtensions:true, noSkills:true, noPromptTemplates:true, noThemes:true, noContextFiles:true, systemPrompt: ROLE_PROMPT, appendSystemPromptOverride: () => []})` then `await loader.reload()`.
- Only ONE command (`/discover`) is needed; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls live in its handler, not in registered model tools.
- Emit progress via ctx.ui.setStatus/setWidget/notify; write the final Markdown note from the handler with plain Node fs (optionally withFileMutationQueue).

5) SUBAGENT / TASK / DELEGATION FACILITY
=====================================================================
NONE built in. Checked: grep `subagent|Subagent|delegate|spawnAgent|ChildSession|childSession` across SDK/dist/**/*.d.ts returned only doc comments like "Override these to delegate command execution to remote systems (for example SSH)" in core/tools/{bash,edit,find,grep,ls,read,write}.d.ts — no type/class/function. `createAgentSession`/`AgentSession` expose no child-session API.

(null = unsupported level); input: ("text"|"image")[] (vision = includes("image")); cost; contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number; samplingParams?; headers?; compat?. If multiple extensions return this, they are chained." (BeforeAgentStartEventResult, types.d.ts:846-849; event exposes systemPrompt + systemPromptOptions, :544-548).

  noSkills?: boolean;          // :78

=====================================================================
8) COMPACTION + HISTORY
=====================================================================
Compaction:
- `session.compact(customInstructions?: string): Promise<CompactionResult>` (agent-session.d.ts:515); abortCompaction(); get isCompacting; get/set autoCompactionEnabled; setAutoCompactionEnabled(enabled).
- Hooks: `on("session_before_compact")` → `{cancel?, compaction?: CompactionResult}` (SessionBeforeCompactEvent/Result, types.d.ts:~460, :857); plus session_compact, session_compact_failed, session_before_tree/session_tree.
- Config: `CompactionSettings { enabled?; reserveTokens?; keepRecentTokens? }` (settings-manager.d.ts:5-8); `getCompactionSettings()` resolves to {enabled, reserveTokens, keepRecentTokens}; `DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SETTINGS` (compaction/compaction.d.ts:40). Set via SettingsManager.inMemory({compaction:{...}}) or setCompactionEnabled(). BranchSummarySettings {reserveTokens?, skipPrompt?}.
- Pure helpers exported: compact(), prepareCompaction(), generateSummary(), shouldCompact(), estimateTokens(), getLastAssistantUsage().

History read — extensions get `ReadonlySessionManager` via ctx (Pick list, session-manager.d.ts:~152): getCwd, getSessionDir, getSessionId, getSessionFile, getLeafId, getLeafEntry, getEntry, getLabel, getBranch, buildContextEntries, getHeader, getEntries, getTree, getSessionName. `buildSessionContext(): SessionContext` resolves compaction-aware messages.
History write — host session: pi.appendEntry(customType, data) (state, not LLM context), pi.sendMessage(...) (LLM context + TUI), pi.sendUserMessage(...), pi.setSessionName, pi.setLabel. Direct: `SessionManager` (session-manager.d.ts:194+) appendMessage/appendCustomEntry/appendCustomMessageEntry/appendCompaction/appendBranchSummary/appendModelChange/appendThinkingLevelChange/appendLabelChange/appendSessionInfo/branch/resetLeaf/createBranchedSession; statics create/open/continueRecent/inMemory/forkFrom/list/listAll.

=====================================================================
9) CONCURRENT / BATCH REQUESTS
=====================================================================
No SDK-level batch API, request queue, or global rate-limit governor (nothing in dist typings; queue matches are only SteeringQueue/FollowUpQueue for message delivery).
What exists:
- Tool-call parallelism: agent-loop default `toolExecution: "parallel"` — sibling tool calls preflighted sequentially then executed concurrently (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:22, :232; docs/extensions.md:655-658, :784).
- Per-request retry/backoff inside provider adapters: `retryProviderRequest(...)` honoring Retry-After and 408/409/429/5xx; options maxRetries, maxRetryDelayMs, signal (PI_AI/dist/api/*.js; google-shared.d.ts:74-82). Agent-turn auto-retry is separate (auto_retry_* events; RetrySettings in settings-manager.d.ts:17-22).
- Fan-out is user-implemented: create N AgentSessions (or N model calls) with your own concurrency cap — subagent's `mapWithConcurrencyLimit` with MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 is the reference (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:5-6, :220-240).

=====================================================================
10) TOOL LOOP SEMANTICS
=====================================================================
- Loop lives in @earendil-works/pi-agent-core (`agentLoop`/`runAgentLoop`, agent-loop.d.ts). Outer `while (true)` for follow-ups + inner `while (hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0)` (agent-loop.js:84-88).
- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort.
- Abort: Agent.abort() (agent.d.ts), AgentSession.abort() (agent-session.d.ts:444), ctx.abort() (types.d.ts:1301), and AbortSignal passed to tools/streams (options.signal, execute(..., signal, ...)).
- Tool result feedback: toolcall_end → execute → AgentToolResult → tool_result/tool_execution_end events → toolResult message appended to context → next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). ToolResultEventResult can replace content/details/isError/usage; terminate:true on every finalized batch result stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on AgentLoopConfig (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / AgentOptions (agent.d.ts): shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean, prepareNextTurn(context), getSteeringMessages(), getFollowUpMessages(), beforeToolCall ({block:true}), afterToolCall (override), toolExecution.
- Extension running its own loop: (a) call session.prompt() repeatedly; (b) construct your own Agent and drive prompt()/continue() with custom hooks; (c) skip the agent and call modelRuntime.complete()/stream() per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover.

=====================================================================
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE pi-discover REWRITE
=====================================================================
- Extension can own orchestration: `ModelRuntime.create()` once (or reuse host context), then per role `modelRuntime.complete(model, {systemPrompt, messages, tools?}, {signal, ...})` — stateless and concurrent; auth handled by the host if you reuse the host ModelRuntime. No AgentSession needed when roles don't need tool loops.
- If roles need tools/sessions: `createAgentSession({modelRuntime, model, resourceLoader, tools, customTools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(...)})` per role; run with Promise.all + your own concurrency cap (e.g. 4).
- Isolate each role's prompt/discovery: `new DefaultResourceLoader({cwd, agentDir, noExtensions:true, noSkills:true, noPromptTemplates:true, noThemes:true, noContextFiles:true, systemPrompt: ROLE_PROMPT, appendSystemPromptOverride: () => []})` then `await loader.reload()`.
- Only ONE command (`/discover`) is needed; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls live in its handler, not in registered model tools.
- Emit progress via ctx.ui.setStatus/setWidget/notify; write the final Markdown note from the handler with plain Node fs (optionally withFileMutationQueue)."}, "error": null, "type": null}

data.architecture: Two distinct execution paths exist. (A) Host-owned session: the host builds an AgentSession from CreateAgentSessionOptions (model runtime + ResourceLoader + SessionManager + SettingsManager + tool allowlist); extensions attach to it only through event hooks and a read-only SessionManager, and commands run inside that session's lifecycle. (B) Extension-owned sessions: an extension can call createAgentSession() N times to get fully independent AgentSession objects (each with its own Agent, transcript, and event stream), sharing one ModelRuntime for auth/model resolution — this is the supported way to run concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls in one process. A third, lower-level path is calling modelRuntime.stream()/complete() directly with a Context {systemPrompt, messages, tools} for stateless single-shot model calls without an agent loop. There is no SDK-level orchestration/subagent primitive: delegation is implemented by either creating multiple AgentSessions or spawning the `pi` subprocess (see examples/extensions/subagent).

=====================================================================
No SDK-level batch API, request queue, or global rate-limit governor (nothing in dist typings; queue matches are only SteeringQueue/FollowUpQueue for message delivery).
What exists:
- Tool-call parallelism: agent-loop default `toolExecution: "parallel"` — sibling tool calls preflighted sequentially then executed concurrently (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:22, :232; docs/extensions.md:655-658, :784).
- Per-request retry/backoff inside provider adapters: `retryProviderRequest(...)` honoring Retry-After and 408/409/429/5xx; options maxRetries, maxRetryDelayMs, signal (PI_AI/dist/api/*.js; google-shared.d.ts:74-82). Agent-turn auto-retry is separate (auto_retry_* events; RetrySettings in settings-manager.d.ts:17-22).
- Fan-out is user-implemented: create N AgentSessions (or N model calls) with your own concurrency cap — subagent's `mapWithConcurrencyLimit` with MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 is the reference (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:5-6, :220-240).

=====================================================================
10) TOOL LOOP SEMANTICS
=====================================================================
- Loop lives in @earendil-works/pi-agent-core (`agentLoop`/`runAgentLoop`, agent-loop.d.ts). Outer `while (true)` for follow-ups + inner `while (hasMoreToolCalls || pendingMessages.length > 0)` (agent-loop.js:84-88).
- MAX ITERATIONS: none. Grep for `maxIterations|maxTurns|maxSteps` across PI_AGENT/dist/**/*.d.ts returned NO option; the loop is unbounded and terminates on no-more-tool-calls / early-termination / abort.
- Abort: Agent.abort() (agent.d.ts), AgentSession.abort() (agent-session.d.ts:444), ctx.abort() (types.d.ts:1301), and AbortSignal passed to tools/streams (options.signal, execute(..., signal, ...)).
- Tool result feedback: toolcall_end → execute → AgentToolResult → tool_result/tool_execution_end events → toolResult message appended to context → next LLM call (docs/sdk.md:249-333). ToolResultEventResult can replace content/details/isError/usage; terminate:true on every finalized batch result stops after that batch (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:317-331).
- Loop control hooks on AgentLoopConfig (PI_AGENT types.d.ts:~180-260) / AgentOptions (agent.d.ts): shouldStopAfterTurn(context): boolean, prepareNextTurn(context), getSteeringMessages(), getFollowUpMessages(), beforeToolCall ({block:true}), afterToolCall (override), toolExecution.
- Extension running its own loop: (a) call session.prompt() repeatedly; (b) construct your own Agent and drive prompt()/continue() with custom hooks; (c) skip the agent and call modelRuntime.complete()/stream() per request in a loop you control (planner → N researchers in parallel → synthesizer). (c) is the cleanest fit for pi-discover.

=====================================================================
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE pi-discover REWRITE
=====================================================================
- Extension can own orchestration: `ModelRuntime.create()` once (or reuse host context), then per role `modelRuntime.complete(model, {systemPrompt, messages, tools?}, {signal, ...})` — stateless and concurrent; auth handled by the host if you reuse the host ModelRuntime. No AgentSession needed when roles don't need tool loops.
- If roles need tools/sessions: `createAgentSession({modelRuntime, model, resourceLoader, tools, customTools, sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(), settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory(...)})` per role; run with Promise.all + your own concurrency cap (e.g. 4).
- Isolate each role's prompt/discovery: `new DefaultResourceLoader({cwd, agentDir, noExtensions:true, noSkills:true, noPromptTemplates:true, noThemes:true, noContextFiles:true, systemPrompt: ROLE_PROMPT, appendSystemPromptOverride: () => []})` then `await loader.reload()`.
- Only ONE command (`/discover`) is needed; the concurrent planner/researcher/synthesizer calls live in its handler, not in registered model tools.
- Emit progress via ctx.ui.setStatus/setWidget/notify; write the final Markdown note from the handler with plain Node fs (optionally withFileMutationQueue).

=====================================================================
5) SUBAGENT / TASK / DELEGATION FACILITY
=====================================================================
NONE built in. Checked: grep `subagent|Subagent|delegate|spawnAgent|ChildSession|childSession` across SDK/dist/**/*.d.ts returned only doc comments like "Override these to delegate command execution to remote systems (for example SSH)" in core/tools/{bash,edit,find,grep,ls,read,write}.d.ts — no type/class/function. `createAgentSession`/`AgentSession` expose no child-session API.

- Only shipped delegation is an EXAMPLE: SDK/examples/extensions/subagent/ — a tool that spawns a separate `pi` child process via `node:child_process` with args `["--mode","json","-p","--no-session", ...]`, parses JSONL events (`message_end`, `tool_result_end`) from stdout, supports single/parallel/chain modes with MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS=8, MAX_CONCURRENCY=4, propagates AbortSignal by killing the child (index.ts:8-20, :300-420).
So: in-process delegate = create N AgentSessions yourself; process-isolated = spawn `pi --mode json -p`. No `Task` tool or agent-of-agents type.

6) MODEL REGISTRY / PROVIDER API
=====================================================================
A) `ModelRuntime implements Models` (dist/core/model-runtime.d.ts:35) — async, canonical, does auth:

B) `ModelRegistry` (dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:18) — SYNC facade exposed as `ctx.modelRegistry`:

   getApiKeyAndHeaders(model): Promise<ResolvedRequestAuth>; getProviderAuthStatus(provider); getProvider(provider);
